Make a set of exercises from the chapters of Robert Hutchinson's
[*Music Theory for the 21st-Century Classroom*](https://musictheory.pugetsound.edu/mt21c/MusicTheory.html) you choose. Answer them here
and press **Check my answers**, or **Print worksheet** for class (tick *with the answer key* for a copy with answers on a page of its own).

**Sharing a set:** the questions come from the number in the link (`seed`). Copy **Link to this set** and everyone who opens it gets the
same questions. **New set** makes different ones.

**The chorales** are made by the site, not taken from real music: four voices, four-bar phrases, using the chords of the chapters you
chose and the ones before them. Every one is checked for voice-leading errors before it's shown. **Writing notes:** type each note with
its octave (middle C is C4), e.g. `E4 D4 C#4`. Your notes appear in the score as you type.

<div id="ex-builder"></div>

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## For teachers

- **Chapters** set the chords in the chorales (up to the highest chapter ticked, favouring the ones ticked: 7 triads and cadences, 8 seventh
  chords, 16 inversions and the cadential 6/4, 17 secondary dominants, 18 secondary diminished chords, 19 mixture, 20 the Neapolitan), and
  which drill questions appear. Periods need chapter 13. Augmented sixths (21) and jazz (31) appear as drill questions, not in chorales.
- **Roman numerals** are checked against the generator's analysis, in the book's figures (V65, I6, iiø7, V7/V, vii°7/V, N6, ♭VI). The
  cadential 6/4 is labelled I64 (i64); Cad64 and V64 are also accepted.
- **Cadences** are read from the voiced chorale (7.4): PAC needs V or V7 to I, both in root position, with the tonic in the soprano;
  otherwise V or vii° to I is an IAC.
- **Periods** (13.3): the first cadence weaker (HC or IAC) than the second (PAC). Parallel when the two phrases begin with the same bars,
  contrasting otherwise. Two phrases ending PAC count as "not a period". The book's other combinations (double periods, phrase groups,
  elisions) aren't generated.
- **Writing a voice:** any answer without voice-leading errors in its bars (ranges, crossing, spacing, parallel 5ths and octaves,
  doubling the leading tone or a 7th, a chord with no root or 3rd) counts. Unresolved leading tones and 7ths, and direct 5ths and octaves,
  are pointed out but not marked wrong. One good answer is in the key.
- **Notation answers:** typed into the exercise for now. The choice of input is a setting (`input=` in the link), so the Notation page
  can be added as another way in.
- **Checked:** `node tests/lessons/exercises.test.js` (thousands of chorales through the voice-leading checker, which is itself tested on
  planted errors) and `node tests/lessons/exercise-builder.cdp.js` (the page).
:::
